title: Blood culture
what: Blood is taken from a vein into special bottles. The lab watches whether germs grow in it.
why: For a high fever and a possible infection in the blood. It is usually done in hospital.
duration: the draw takes 5 to 10 minutes; a first answer usually comes in 1 to 3 days, the final one in up to 5 to 7 days
tell_doctor: If you are allergic to antiseptic or iodine
If you already have an IV line in a vein

prepare.title: Antibiotics
prepare.text: It is best to take the sample before the first antibiotic dose. But treatment is not delayed. The doctor decides.

prepare.title: Timing
prepare.text: Blood is often taken at the peak of a fever or during chills.

bring: Your referral, if done as an outpatient
steps: The skin on your arm is cleaned with antiseptic for a long time and very carefully
A band is tightened above your elbow
Blood is drawn into 2 bottles, sometimes from both arms
The needle comes out, and a cotton pad is pressed on
The bottles go to the lab right away
feel: A quick prick, like a pinch
From both arms means two pricks
after: Press the cotton pad for 3 to 5 minutes
A first answer usually comes in 1 to 3 days, the full one in up to a week
If a germ grows, the lab checks which antibiotics work on it
red_flags: Chills, a fever over 39°C (102°F), confusion, or strong weakness: call emergency services

faq.q: Why take blood from both arms?
faq.a: It makes it easier to tell a real infection from a stray germ from the skin.
Some germs grow slowly. While waiting, treatment has usually already started.

reminders.text: Blood culture soon. If you started antibiotics, be sure to tell the nurse.
